newsitem.title: USA: Minn. seeding pace tops average but emergence slow.
newsitem.headline: Minn. seeding pace tops average but emergence slow.

text.p: Corn and soybean plantings were ahead of the average pace in the week ended Sunday but cool, dry weather slowed germination, according to the Minnesota Agricultural Statistics Service.
Corn was 97 percent seeded, versus 77 percent last year and 85 percent for the five-year average. But 46 percent of the crop had emerged, against 52 percent on average.
Soybeans were 82 percent planted, against 32 percent last year and 58 percent for the five-year average. Emergence reached eight percent, off the five-year average of 20 percent.

Spring wheat was 66 percent planted, trailing the five-year average of 80 percent. The crop was rated 23 percent very poor, four percent poor, 24 percent fair, 45 percent good and four percent excellent.
"Soil temperatures are below seasonal normals, and recently planted fields have had scant moisture for germinating seeds," the weekly update said.
Topsoil moisture was rated seven percent very short, 30 percent short, 55 percent adequate and eight percent surplus.
Pasture was rated seven percent very poor, 27 percent poor, 40 fair, 24 good and two percent excellent.
